$comment: Pins the shipped Go and TypeScript HDF validators to one another on the closure of `extensions`. `extensions` is a closed, defined object: its members are `passthrough` (the deliberately permissive catch-all) and `rawSourceArtifacts`. Anything else a producer wants to carry goes inside `passthrough`. Both halves of this repo read this file and validate the same documents at both the sites `extensions` appears — the document root and `baselines[]` — so they cannot disagree about whether a document is valid HDF. Closure is written as `additionalProperties: false` rather than the house `unevaluatedProperties: false` because the Go validator is a draft-07 engine that does not implement the latter; a rule only one validator enforces is not a rule.

cases.name: empty extensions
cases.why: no members is a valid closed object

cases.name: passthrough is permissive inside
cases.why: passthrough imposes no shape on its contents — that is its purpose

cases.name: checklist round-trip metadata under passthrough
cases.why: the ckl/cklb bridge carries its unmodeled fields in passthrough

cases.name: merge provenance under passthrough
cases.why: hdf-engine's merge provenance is unmodeled data like any other

cases.name: undeclared key
cases.why: extensions is closed — an unmodeled key belongs in passthrough, not beside it

cases.name: undeclared key beside a defined member
cases.why: a valid member does not license an invalid sibling

cases.name: legacy v1 provenance left at the top
cases.why: the legacy converter's version marker moved into passthrough

cases.name: merge provenance left at the top
cases.why: HDF's own tooling gets no exemption from the closure

cases.name: rawSourceArtifacts is not an array
cases.why: a single artifact still travels in the array

cases.name: passthrough is not an object
cases.why: permissive about keys, not about type
